screened.motion: This house believes every multi-agent system should have a designated lead agent.
screened.why: Both conclude that a deliberately chosen lead beats leadership emerging by accident in coordination-heavy systems, and that simple parallel tasks can do without one: Claude calls a lead a sensible default rather than a rule, and Gemini limits its claim to "almost any serious" system.

screened.motion: This house believes a team that cannot show the return on its AI coding spend should cut it.
screened.why: Both agree that unmeasured AI spend is a governance failure and that bigger PRs aren't real productivity, but they part ways on the motion itself: Claude says cutting is the wrong fix and the team should cap spend while it builds a measure, while Gemini wants the tools turned off until they show a return.

motion: This house believes a team that cannot show the return on its AI coding spend should cut it.
why: Editor's check: In its first debate turn Gemini says as fact that firms spend "up to $1,500 per developer monthly", but the brief gives higher figures: about $1,600 at the quant firm and about $3,000 at the two-person agency.
alt: The Motion, Motion 4. This house believes a team that cannot show the return on its AI coding spend should cut it. Claude, after arguing against, alone: "In the room I read "cut" as cutting to zero, and I scored a point by saying Gemini had come round to my position."
